pr.title: Tell every session on an S3 location when its credentials lapse
pr.head: 75dcfa3c51b6997aa1605d751ebe4a0cee1cddfc

summary: Projector carries messages between your agent sessions through a relay location. An S3 location stores those encrypted records in a bucket, and the daemon signs each request with your AWS credentials. Until this layer, a credential failure stopped delivery with an explanation available only through status commands.

This layer adds one notice to the location’s repository inbox on the affected machine. Every session using that location can see it. A changed failure reason replaces the same notice, dismissing it hides it until recovery, and a successful signed request withdraws it. The notice stays on this machine and is never sent to the bucket.

The reviewed head is clean. All four earlier findings are fixed: a busy mirror is retried, both interfaces omit Snooze, interrupted writes retain a recoverable notice ID, and local dismissal needs no relay key. The full configured gate and focused regression checks pass.

cards.title: Terms used on this page
cards.html:
• Location: the endpoint, bucket, and prefix shared by a group of sessions.
  • Mirror: the local numbered copies that the inbox, panel, and console display.
  • Local notice: a Projector-generated entry held only in that mirror, with no corresponding bucket record.
  • Signed request: an S3 operation authenticated with AWS credentials.

cards.title: What was checked
cards.html:
• Local plugin validation, 256 hook tests, type-checking, and diff validation passed.
  • The exact-head CI check passed.
  • 189 focused notice, repository-console, inbox, and peer tests passed. The console dismissal case also passed with an empty temporary home.
  • An independent failed final metadata write retained the notice ID; retry reused one entry and recovery removed it.
  • The real two-machine bucket check remains deferred until after merge; no cloud service was contacted during this review.

groups.title: A notice has its own entry role
groups.kicker: The panel can distinguish a machine-local notice from peer traffic.
intro: The repository inbox already distinguishes incoming items, copies of items you sent, and replies. The new local role represents Projector’s own notice about the relay location. It has the notice kind, takes a dismissal, and carries no response back to a peer.

files.note: Adds the local role to the entry shape shared by the panel’s inbox code.

groups.title: Keep one local notice in the mirror
groups.kicker: A separate metadata file remembers the notice and its dismissal.
intro: A mirror is the local store of numbered repository-inbox entries. The new functions post, replace, dismiss, and withdraw one local notice per location. Its metadata records a stable random ID before the entry can appear, then records the text after the mirror write succeeds. A lock timeout can therefore delay the notice without either suppressing it or losing its identity.

The same module renders the entry as a notice from Projector on this machine and refuses responses and snoozes. It routes local changes through change_local, which dismisses the notice without reading an encryption key because it sends nothing. The CLI and console call this path before the ordinary relay-key lookup.

files.note: Persists the local notice lifecycle, refuses relayed actions, and adds its inbox display text.

checks.text: Injected a failure in the final metadata write after the mirror already held the notice. The earlier ID write remained durable, a retry reused one entry, and withdrawal removed it. The daemon interruption and busy-lock regression tests also pass.
The console dispatches the local entry before sealing_key. The dismissal regression passed both with the credential boundary returning no key and in an empty temporary home.

groups.title: Connect notices to credential failures and recovery
groups.kicker: The relay job posts after its work and withdraws after authenticated success.
intro: An S3 transport sends the bucket requests for one relay job. This layer records whether a signed operation succeeds, even if the store’s capability probe later refuses to use the bucket. That distinction lets the job remove a credential notice once the credentials work again.

The job posts or withdraws the notice on its worker thread after it saves the relay cache. It also excludes local entries from pruning, because they have no bucket record whose disappearance could mean they were dismissed elsewhere.

files.note: Tracks authenticated success, updates the local notice after each S3 job, and preserves it during mirror pruning.

checks.text: The pruning filter excludes the local role. The lapse lifecycle tests passed, including recovery withdrawal and a later failure showing the notice again.

files.note: Adds credential-process failure modes and two daemon-to-inbox lifecycle tests.

checks.text: Ran all five LapseNoticeTests cases within the 189-test focused run. They cover replacement, dismissal, recovery, a busy mirror, interruption after mirroring, and CLI dismissal with no relay key.

groups.title: Keep local controls and commands independent of relay keys
groups.kicker: The panel and console hide Snooze; command dispatch dismisses without encryption.
intro: The Claude Code panel and terminal console draw the repository inbox beside a session’s own items and pull requests. A local notice uses the existing row and drawer, but both action lists omit Snooze. Dismiss uses the corresponding local change path rather than the peer-response path.

The CLI now recognizes the local role before looking up the relay key. Both the console and CLI can dismiss this machine’s notice while that key is absent or unreadable. Their regression tests exercise the visible outcome with no key available.

files.note: Omits Snooze when the displayed repository entry has the local role.

checks.text: The configured gate ran the new panel test among 256 passing hook tests. It confirmed no Snooze button and one dismiss command for the local notice.

files.note: Exercises the local notice’s visible controls and emitted dismissal command.
Omits Snooze for the local role in the terminal console’s action list.

checks.text: The updated control dispatch and repository-console tests confirm that a local notice’s drawer offers Dismiss and no Snooze.

files.note: Exercises local-notice controls and successful dismissal while the relay key is unavailable.

checks.text: This regression now passes with command_key returning no key. It also passed in a fresh temporary home, where the previous head failed its final removal assertion.

files.note: Dispatches local notices before relay-key lookup and prints a machine-local dismissal result.

checks.text: The new CLI regression passes with no relay key: dismiss returns success, removes the notice from both sessions’ shared mirror, and sends no relay state.

groups.title: Document the notice and record project completion
groups.kicker: The reference describes the lifecycle; the plan records evidence and the deferred real-bucket check.
intro: The CLI reference explains how you hear about a credential failure, how to dismiss the notice, and when recovery removes it. The S3 project plan records the local-notice design and marks the four-layer implementation completed.

The outcome maps acceptance criteria to automated tests. It explicitly leaves the two-machine exchange through a real bucket for the user after merge, with delivery timing to be recorded in the plan afterward.

files.note: Adds the credential-notice example and its machine-local dismissal and withdrawal rules.
